# ml-symbolic-regression: deep theory context

This context is grounded in the local symbolic-regression sources `1905.13266-epsilon-lexicase.tar`, `1912.04871-deep-symbolic-regression.tar`, and `1905.11481-ai-feynman.tar`. The common mathematical theme is that symbolic regression is not only function approximation. It is structured search over a compositional expression language, with an implicit prior over algebraic simplicity, symmetries, and per-case behavioral niches.

## Search space and description-length pressure

Let an expression tree $T$ be generated by a grammar with terminals $x_1,\ldots,x_d,c_1,\ldots,c_m$ and primitives such as $+,\times,\div,\sin,\exp,\log$. The program denotes a partial function $f_T:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ after protected or domain-restricted evaluation. On data $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$, define the empirical risk and structural cost

$$
\hat L(T)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \ell(f_T(x_i),y_i),
\qquad
C(T)=\sum_{v\in T} c(\mathrm{op}(v)).
$$

A compact way to write the complexity pressure present in symbolic-regression search is a description-length-style score

$$
\mathcal E_\beta(T)=\hat L(T)+\beta C(T),
\qquad
p_\beta(T\mid D)\propto \exp[-n\hat L(T)-\beta C(T)].
$$

The constant $\beta$ controls the exchange rate between fit and expression complexity. In symbolic regression this exchange rate can be delayed or made local: too much early parsimony removes expressions that are temporarily large because they contain reusable subterms. Epsilon lexicase and AI Feynman both preserve behaviorally useful partial structure before final simplification.

Complexity can be treated as a prior over equivalence classes, not raw syntax. Algebraic identities create many trees for the same function:

$$
x(x+1) \equiv x^2+x,
\qquad
\log(ab)\equiv \log a+\log b.
$$

If $[T]$ is the semantic equivalence class of $T$ on the target domain, the complexity prior can be written over the simplest representative,

$$
C_{\mathrm{sem}}([T])=\min_{T'\in [T]} C(T').
$$

This motivates simplification, canonicalization, dimensional analysis, and separability tests as structural operations rather than postprocessing utilities.

## Error-vector geometry and lexicase selection

The epsilon-lexicase source frames selection through per-case errors rather than aggregate fitness. Each program has an error vector

$$
e(T)=(e_1(T),\ldots,e_n(T))\in\mathbb R_+^n.
$$

Aggregate symbolic regression collapses this vector to a scalar

$$
\bar e(T)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e_i(T),
$$

which erases which cases a program solves. Exact lexicase samples a case order $\pi$ and repeatedly filters

$$
S_k=\{T\in S_{k-1}:e_{\pi_k}(T)=\min_{U\in S_{k-1}}e_{\pi_k}(U)\}.
$$

For a fixed $\pi$, this is lexicographic minimization of the ordered vector $(e_{\pi_1},\ldots,e_{\pi_n})$. Epsilon lexicase replaces equality to the best error by membership in an acceptance band. With threshold $\tau_j$, the filter is

$$
S_k=\{T\in S_{k-1}:e_{\pi_k}(T)\le \tau_{\pi_k}(S_{k-1})\}.
$$

As a derived formalization of the source selection rule, the selection probability of a program is a probability over random lexicographic cones:

$$
p_{\mathrm{lex}}(T)=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi}
\mathbb P(T\text{ is chosen from }S_n(\pi)).
$$

This nonlinear selection rule is important because symbolic expressions often contain regime specialists. If the target decomposes as

$$
y=f^\star(x)=
\begin{cases}
g_1(x),&x\in R_1,\\
g_2(x),&x\in R_2,
\end{cases}
$$

a candidate matching $g_1$ but not $g_2$ has poor mean error yet contains scientific structure. Lexicase can select it when cases from $R_1$ appear early. A scalar objective would suppress it unless explicit niching is added.

## Epsilon thresholds as robust local scale

For regression errors, exact equality is too brittle. The epsilon-lexicase source studies thresholds based on the median absolute deviation. For a case $j$, let

$$
m_j=\mathrm{median}_{T\in P} e_j(T),
\qquad
\lambda_j=\mathrm{median}_{T\in P}|e_j(T)-m_j|.
$$

The elite-relative threshold has the form

$$
\tau_j=e_j^\star+\lambda_j,
\qquad
e_j^\star=\min_{T\in P}e_j(T).
$$

This is a robust scale rule. If a few expressions explode because of division, logarithms, or exponentials, the standard deviation can be dominated by invalid or extreme outputs. The MAD threshold only changes when a large fraction of the population changes. A quantile threshold has a related form:

$$
\tau_j=e_j^\star+Q_\alpha\{|e_j(T)-m_j|:T\in P\},
$$

where $\alpha$ controls how many near-elites survive each case. The expected filter strength is

$$
q_j(\tau_j)=\frac{1}{|P|}\sum_{T\in P}\mathbb I\{e_j(T)\le \tau_j\}.
$$

Assuming approximate independence of filters, the expected surviving set after $k$ cases is

$$
\mathbb E|S_k|\approx |P|\prod_{\ell=1}^k q_{\pi_\ell}(\tau_{\pi_\ell}).
$$

The goal is not to make $q_j$ uniformly small. The goal is to let hard or informative cases filter sharply while preventing continuous-noise accidents from making selection depend on one infinitesimal error difference.

## Pareto view and approximate nondominance

Treat each training case as an objective. Program $A$ dominates program $B$ if

$$
e_i(A)\le e_i(B)\ \text{for all }i,
\qquad
e_j(A)<e_j(B)\ \text{for at least one }j.
$$

Exact lexicase selects from nondominated regions of this many-objective space. Epsilon lexicase selects from approximate nondominated regions, replacing hard coordinate comparisons by tolerance bands. A useful theorem-style statement is:

If $B$ is selected by exact lexicase under order $\pi$ and $A$ strictly dominates $B$, then $A$ survives every filter survived by $B$ and eliminates $B$ at the first coordinate where $A$ is strictly better. Therefore $B$ cannot be selected. Thus exact lexicase-selected programs are Pareto nondominated, up to tie-breaking.

The converse is false: high-dimensional Pareto fronts can be huge. Lexicase imposes randomized sparse scalarizations without forming a weighted sum. This is valuable for symbolic regression because a good scientific expression may first appear as a specialist on a sparse subset of cases where a latent mechanism is isolated.

## Deep symbolic regression as policy search

The deep symbolic regression source casts expression generation as sequential decision making. A recurrent policy samples a token sequence $\tau=(a_1,\ldots,a_T)$ that builds a valid expression. Let $R(\tau)$ be a reward based on prediction error and possibly complexity. The policy objective is

$$
J(\theta)=\mathbb E_{\tau\sim p_\theta}[R(\tau)].
$$

The score-function gradient is

$$
\nabla_\theta J(\theta)=
\mathbb E_{\tau\sim p_\theta}
\left[(R(\tau)-b)\nabla_\theta\log p_\theta(\tau)\right],
$$

where $b$ is a baseline. This gives a different search axis from genetic programming: the grammar and reward shape the policy distribution over compositional motifs.

The nontrivial part is that the reward is sparse and many expressions are invalid or redundant. A risk-seeking variant optimizes the upper tail of rewards rather than the mean. If $R_\epsilon(\theta)$ is the $(1-\epsilon)$-quantile reward, the conditional objective is

$$
J_\epsilon(\theta)=
\mathbb E_\theta[R(\tau)\mid R(\tau)\ge R_\epsilon(\theta)].
$$

This is aligned with symbolic discovery: one excellent formula matters more than improving the average sampled formula. The search prior can be strengthened by adding complexity and physical constraints inside the reward:

$$
R(T)=-\log(\hat L(T)+\delta)-\beta C(T)-\rho V_{\mathrm{domain}}(T),
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{domain}}$ penalizes dimensional inconsistency, invalid domains, or nonfinite evaluation. These penalties enter the scalar reward optimized by the score-function estimator even when the expression evaluator is discrete.

## Compositional symmetries from AI Feynman

The AI Feynman source emphasizes that physical formulas often have hidden simplicity: separability, compositionality, symmetries, dimensional constraints, and low-dimensional structure. These are not generic ML heuristics; they induce algebraic tests that reduce search dimension.

Additive separability means there is a partition $x=(u,v)$ such that

$$
f(u,v)=g(u)+h(v).
$$

Then mixed partial derivatives vanish:

$$
\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial u_a\partial v_b}=0
\quad\text{for all }a,b.
$$

Multiplicative separability means

$$
f(u,v)=g(u)h(v).
$$

Where $f$ is nonzero, this becomes additive separability after a logarithm:

$$
\log|f(u,v)|=\log|g(u)|+\log|h(v)|.
$$

This gives an operational test: fit a smooth surrogate $\hat f$, estimate cross-derivatives or finite-difference interaction residuals, and split the search if the interaction tensor has small norm.

Translational symmetry in variable $x_j$ has the form

$$
f(x_1,\ldots,x_j+a,\ldots,x_d)=f(x)+c(a)
$$

or, for invariance, $c(a)=0$. Scale symmetry has the form

$$
f(x_1,\ldots,\alpha x_j,\ldots,x_d)=\alpha^p f(x)
$$

or a compensating transformation across several variables. If a formula is homogeneous with exponents $p_1,\ldots,p_d$,

$$
f(\alpha^{p_1}x_1,\ldots,\alpha^{p_d}x_d)=\alpha^q f(x).
$$

Differentiating at $\alpha=1$ gives the Euler-type constraint

$$
\sum_{j=1}^d p_j x_j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}=q f(x).
$$

This converts symmetry discovery into linear regression on derivative features. Once a symmetry is found, one can form invariants and search in fewer variables.

## Dimensional analysis as a null-space computation

AI Feynman also uses dimensional analysis. Suppose each variable $x_j$ has dimension vector $d_j\in\mathbb R^r$ over base units, and the target has dimension $d_y$. Let $D=[d_1,\ldots,d_d]$. A monomial $\prod_j x_j^{a_j}$ has dimension $Da$. A dimensionless invariant satisfies

$$
Da=0.
$$

A prefactor matching the target satisfies

$$
Da=d_y.
$$

If $a_0$ is one solution of $Da=d_y$ and $N$ spans the null space of $D$, then all dimensionally valid monomial prefactors are

$$
a=a_0+Nz.
$$

The Buckingham-style reduction is

$$
y=\prod_j x_j^{a_{0j}}\ \phi(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k),
\qquad
\pi_\ell=\prod_j x_j^{N_{j\ell}}.
$$

The reduced symbolic-regression target is then $\phi$, not the original $d$-variable expression. The grammar is quotient by dimensional invariance before expensive search begins.

## Algebraic decomposition as recursive risk factorization

A generic symbolic-regression algorithm searches directly for

$$
\min_T \sum_i \ell(T(x_i),y_i)+\beta C(T).
$$

The AI Feynman view replaces this by recursive factorization. If a transform $\mathcal R$ proves or strongly suggests

$$
f(x)=A(x_S)\circ B(x_{S^c}),
$$

then the search decomposes into lower-dimensional subproblems. For additive structure,

$$
\hat g=\arg\min_g\sum_i \ell(g(x_{i,S}), y_i-\hat h(x_{i,S^c})).
$$

For multiplicative structure with positive outputs,

$$
\widehat{\log g}=\arg\min_u\sum_i \ell(u(x_{i,S}), \log y_i-\widehat{\log h}(x_{i,S^c})).
$$

This recursion changes the heuristic search scaling. If the expression grammar has branching factor $B$ and depth budget $m$, exhaustive search is roughly $B^m$. If a separability test splits one $d$-variable problem into two subproblems with depths $m_1,m_2$ and $m_1+m_2\approx m$, the cost becomes

$$
B^{m_1}+B^{m_2}
$$

rather than $B^m$. The algebraic reason is not just accuracy; the transformations make the combinatorial search additive instead of multiplicative.

# Task: ml-symbolic-regression

# Symbolic Regression: GP Search Strategy

## Objective
Design and implement a better genetic programming search strategy for symbolic regression. Your code goes in `custom_sr.py`. Three reference implementations (Standard GP, Parsimony GP, Lexicase GP) demonstrate different approaches.

## Background
Symbolic regression discovers mathematical expressions that fit data. Genetic programming evolves a population of expression trees through selection, crossover, and mutation. Key challenges include balancing exploration vs exploitation, controlling expression complexity (bloat), and escaping local optima. Different approaches address these through fitness shaping, novel selection mechanisms, or improved genetic operators.

## Evaluation
Tested on three standard symbolic regression benchmarks: Nguyen-7 (univariate transcendental), Nguyen-10 (bivariate trigonometric), Koza-3 (univariate polynomial). Metric: R² on held-out test set (higher is better).

def fitness_function(tree, X, y):
    """Evaluate fitness of a candidate program. Lower is better."""
    y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
    return float(np.mean((y - y_pred) ** 2))


def _per_case_errors(population, X, y):
    """Compute per-case absolute errors for the entire population.
    
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (len(population), n_samples)
    """
    errors = np.empty((len(population), X.shape[0]))
    for i, tree in enumerate(population):
        y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
        errors[i] = np.abs(y - y_pred)
    return errors


def selection(population, fitnesses, n_select, _errors=None, _parsimony_coeff=0.0):
    """Epsilon-lexicase selection with parsimony tie-breaking.
    
    Requires _errors (per-case errors) to be passed via evolve_one_generation.
    If _errors is None, falls back to tournament selection.
    """
    selected = []
    pop_size = len(population)
    
    if _errors is None:
        # Fallback to tournament selection
        tournament_size = 7
        for _ in range(n_select):
            candidates = random.sample(range(pop_size), min(tournament_size, pop_size))
            best = min(candidates, key=lambda i: fitnesses[i])
            selected.append(population[best].copy())
        return selected
    
    n_cases = _errors.shape[1]
    lengths = [tree.size() for tree in population]
    
    for _ in range(n_select):
        candidates = list(range(pop_size))
        cases = list(range(n_cases))
        random.shuffle(cases)
        
        for case in cases:
            if len(candidates) <= 1:
                break
            case_errors = _errors[candidates, case]
            # Epsilon-lexicase with MAD threshold
            min_err = float(np.min(case_errors))
            mad = float(np.median(np.abs(case_errors - float(np.median(case_errors)))))
            candidates = [c for c, e in zip(candidates, case_errors) if e <= min_err + mad]
        
        # Among survivors, apply parsimony pressure: choose smallest tree
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            # Combine fitness and size: penalized fitness = fitness + parsimony_coeff * size
            penalized = [fitnesses[c] + _parsimony_coeff * lengths[c] for c in candidates]
            winner = candidates[int(np.argmin(penalized))]
        else:
            winner = candidates[0]
        selected.append(population[winner].copy())
    
    return selected


def crossover(parent1, parent2, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Standard subtree crossover."""
    offspring = parent1.copy()
    donor = parent2.copy()

    off_size = offspring.size()
    don_size = donor.size()
    if off_size <= 1 or don_size <= 1:
        return offspring

    off_point = random.randint(1, off_size - 1)
    don_point = random.randint(0, don_size - 1)

    donor_nodes = donor.get_all_nodes()
    donor_subtree = donor_nodes[don_point][0].copy()

    off_nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, parent, child_idx = off_nodes[off_point]
    if parent is not None:
        parent.children[child_idx] = donor_subtree
    else:
        offspring = donor_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent1.copy()

    return offspring


def mutation(parent, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Subtree mutation — replace a random subtree with a new random tree."""
    offspring = parent.copy()
    tree_size = offspring.size()
    if tree_size <= 1:
        return generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    mut_point = random.randint(1, tree_size - 1)
    new_subtree = generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, par, child_idx = nodes[mut_point]
    if par is not None:
        par.children[child_idx] = new_subtree
    else:
        offspring = new_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent.copy()

    return offspring


def evolve_one_generation(population, fitnesses, X_train, y_train,
                          n_features, pop_size,
                          crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.05,
                          max_depth=17):
    """Lexicase GP generation with adaptive parsimony pressure.
    
    Combines epsilon-lexicase selection with gplearn-style adaptive
    parsimony coefficient for bloat control.
    """
    new_population = []
    
    # Elitism: keep best individual by raw fitness
    elite_idx = int(np.argmin(fitnesses))
    new_population.append(population[elite_idx].copy())
    
    # Compute per-case errors for lexicase selection
    errors = _per_case_errors(population, X_train, y_train)
    
    # Adaptive parsimony coefficient (gplearn 'auto' method, clamped)
    lengths = np.array([tree.size() for tree in population], dtype=float)
    raw_fit = np.array(fitnesses, dtype=float)
    len_var = float(np.var(lengths))
    if len_var > 1e-15:
        parsimony_coeff = float(np.cov(lengths, raw_fit)[1, 0]) / len_var
        parsimony_coeff = max(parsimony_coeff, 0.0)
        parsimony_coeff = min(parsimony_coeff, 0.001)
    else:
        parsimony_coeff = 0.0
    
    while len(new_population) < pop_size:
        r = random.random()
        if r < crossover_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 2, _errors=errors, _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff)
            child = crossover(parents[0], parents[1], n_features, max_depth)
        elif r < crossover_rate + mutation_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors, _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff)
            child = mutation(parents[0], n_features, max_depth)
        else:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors, _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff)
            child = parents[0]
        new_population.append(child)
    
    return new_population[:pop_size]

def _per_case_errors(population, X, y):
    """Compute per-case absolute errors for the entire population.

        numpy array of shape (len(population), n_samples)
    """
    errors = np.empty((len(population), X.shape[0]))
    for i, tree in enumerate(population):
        y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
        errors[i] = np.abs(y - y_pred)

    Requires _penalized_errors array precomputed in evolve_one_generation.
    Falls back to tournament if not available.

            candidates = random.sample(range(pop_size), min(7, pop_size))

def fitness_function(tree, X, y):
    """MSE fitness — lower is better."""
    y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
    return float(np.mean((y - y_pred) ** 2))


def _per_case_errors(population, X, y):
    """Compute per-case absolute errors for the entire population.

    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (len(population), n_samples)
    """
    errors = np.empty((len(population), X.shape[0]))
    for i, tree in enumerate(population):
        y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
        errors[i] = np.abs(y - y_pred)
    return errors


def _collect_constant_nodes(tree):
    """Return list of (node, parent, child_idx) for constant terminals."""
    nodes = tree.get_all_nodes()
    constant_nodes = []
    for node, parent, child_idx in nodes:
        if node.is_terminal and not isinstance(node.value, str):
            # constant is stored as string, but we can check if numeric
            try:
                float(node.value)
                constant_nodes.append((node, parent, child_idx))
            except ValueError:
                pass
        elif node.is_terminal and node.value.startswith('x'):
            # variable, skip
            pass
        else:
            # might be constant numeric string without 'x'
            try:
                float(node.value)
                constant_nodes.append((node, parent, child_idx))
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return constant_nodes


def _hill_climb_constants(tree, X, y, steps=3, sigma=0.1):
    """Perform simple hill climbing on constants of the tree.
    
    Randomly perturb each constant by Gaussian noise, accept if improves MSE.
    Returns improved tree (copy) and whether any improvement made.
    """
    improved = False
    current_tree = tree.copy()
    current_fitness = fitness_function(current_tree, X, y)
    for _ in range(steps):
        # pick a random constant node
        const_nodes = _collect_constant_nodes(current_tree)
        if not const_nodes:
            break
        node, parent, child_idx = random.choice(const_nodes)
        old_value = float(node.value)
        new_value = old_value + random.gauss(0.0, sigma)
        # clip to reasonable range
        new_value = max(min(new_value, 10.0), -10.0)
        # create new tree with modified constant
        new_tree = current_tree.copy()
        # need to locate the same node in the copy
        # easier: modify in place on current_tree, but we need to keep copy
        # Let's directly modify current_tree's node value (string)
        node.value = str(round(new_value, 4))
        new_fitness = fitness_function(current_tree, X, y)
        if new_fitness < current_fitness:
            current_fitness = new_fitness
            improved = True
            # keep the change
        else:
            # revert
            node.value = str(round(old_value, 4))
    return current_tree, improved


def selection(population, fitnesses, n_select, _errors=None, _penalized_errors=None):
    """Adaptive Parsimony Lexicase selection.

    Uses epsilon-lexicase on penalized per-case errors.
    Requires _penalized_errors array precomputed in evolve_one_generation.
    Falls back to tournament if not available.
    """
    selected = []
    pop_size = len(population)

    if _penalized_errors is None:
        # Fallback to tournament
        for _ in range(n_select):
            candidates = random.sample(range(pop_size), min(7, pop_size))
            best = min(candidates, key=lambda i: fitnesses[i])
            selected.append(population[best].copy())
        return selected

    n_cases = _penalized_errors.shape[1]
    for _ in range(n_select):
        candidates = list(range(pop_size))
        cases = list(range(n_cases))
        random.shuffle(cases)

        for case in cases:
            if len(candidates) <= 1:
                break
            case_errors = _penalized_errors[candidates, case]
            # epsilon-lexicase with adaptive threshold: min_err + MAD
            min_err = float(np.min(case_errors))
            mad = float(np.median(np.abs(case_errors - float(np.median(case_errors)))))
            candidates = [c for c, e in zip(candidates, case_errors) if e <= min_err + mad]

        selected.append(population[winner].copy())

    offspring = parent1.copy()
    donor = parent2.copy()

def evolve_one_generation(population, fitnesses, X_train, y_train,
                          n_features, pop_size,
                          crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.05,
                          max_depth=17):
    """Adaptive Parsimony Lexicase GP generation with constant hill climbing.

    Combines adaptive parsimony coefficient (like parsimony_gp) with
    epsilon-lexicase selection on penalized per-case errors.
    Adds hill climbing on constants for mutated and crossed individuals.
    """
    new_population = []

    # Elitism: keep best by raw fitness
    elite_idx = int(np.argmin(fitnesses))
    new_population.append(population[elite_idx].copy())

    # Adaptive parsimony coefficient (gplearn 'auto' method, clamped)
    lengths = np.array([tree.size() for tree in population], dtype=float)
    raw_fit = np.array(fitnesses, dtype=float)
    len_var = float(np.var(lengths))
    if len_var > 1e-15:
        parsimony_coeff = float(np.cov(lengths, raw_fit)[1, 0]) / len_var
        parsimony_coeff = max(parsimony_coeff, 0.0)
        parsimony_coeff = min(parsimony_coeff, 0.001)
    else:
        parsimony_coeff = 0.0

    # Pre-compute per-case raw errors
    raw_errors = _per_case_errors(population, X_train, y_train)
    # Compute penalized per-case errors: error + parsimony_coeff * size
    # size is same for all cases per individual, broadcast
    penalized_errors = raw_errors + parsimony_coeff * lengths[:, np.newaxis]

    # Hill climbing probability
    hill_climb_prob = 0.5

    while len(new_population) < pop_size:
        r = random.random()
        if r < crossover_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 2, _penalized_errors=penalized_errors)
            child = crossover(parents[0], parents[1], n_features, max_depth)
            # Hill climbing on child
            if random.random() < hill_climb_prob:
                child, _ = _hill_climb_constants(child, X_train, y_train, steps=2)
        elif r < crossover_rate + mutation_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _penalized_errors=penalized_errors)
            child = mutation(parents[0], n_features, max_depth)
            if random.random() < hill_climb_prob:
                child, _ = _hill_climb_constants(child, X_train, y_train, steps=2)
        else:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _penalized_errors=penalized_errors)
            child = parents[0]
            # optional hill climbing on reproduced individual
            if random.random() < hill_climb_prob:
                child, _ = _hill_climb_constants(child, X_train, y_train, steps=2)
        new_population.append(child)

    return new_population[:pop_size]

def fitness_function(tree, X, y):
    """Evaluate fitness of a candidate program. Lower is better."""
    y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
    return float(np.mean((y - y_pred) ** 2))


def _per_case_errors(population, X, y):
    """Compute per-case absolute errors for the entire population.
    
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (len(population), n_samples)
    """
    errors = np.empty((len(population), X.shape[0]))
    for i, tree in enumerate(population):
        y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
        errors[i] = np.abs(y - y_pred)
    return errors


def _compute_novelty_scores(errors, k=10):
    """Compute novelty scores based on Euclidean distance in error space.
    
    Returns:
        list of novelty scores (higher = more novel)
    """
    pop_size = errors.shape[0]
    # Normalize errors per case to zero mean, unit variance (robust)
    eps = 1e-10
    case_median = np.median(errors, axis=0)
    case_mad = np.median(np.abs(errors - case_median), axis=0)
    case_mad[case_mad < eps] = eps
    norm_errors = (errors - case_median) / case_mad
    
    # Compute distances (upper triangle only)
    distances = np.zeros((pop_size, pop_size))
    for i in range(pop_size):
        diff = norm_errors[i] - norm_errors[i+1:, :]
        dist = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff ** 2, axis=1))
        distances[i, i+1:] = dist
        distances[i+1:, i] = dist
    
    # Novelty = average distance to k nearest neighbors
    novelty = np.zeros(pop_size)
    for i in range(pop_size):
        sorted_dists = np.sort(distances[i])
        # exclude self (distance zero)
        nearest = sorted_dists[1:min(k+1, pop_size)]
        novelty[i] = np.mean(nearest) if len(nearest) > 0 else 0.0
    return novelty.tolist()


def selection(population, fitnesses, n_select, _errors=None, _parsimony_coeff=0.0,
              _case_order=None, _novelty_scores=None):
    """Enhanced epsilon-lexicase selection with difficulty ordering and novelty.
    
    Args:
        _errors: per-case error matrix
        _parsimony_coeff: coefficient for size penalty
        _case_order: list of case indices sorted by difficulty (hardest first)
        _novelty_scores: list of novelty scores for each individual
    """
    selected = []
    pop_size = len(population)
    
    if _errors is None:
        # Fallback to tournament selection
        tournament_size = 7
        for _ in range(n_select):
            candidates = random.sample(range(pop_size), min(tournament_size, pop_size))
            best = min(candidates, key=lambda i: fitnesses[i])
            selected.append(population[best].copy())
        return selected
    
    n_cases = _errors.shape[1]
    lengths = [tree.size() for tree in population]
    
    # Default case order: random
    if _case_order is None:
        _case_order = list(range(n_cases))
    
    # Default novelty scores: zeros
    if _novelty_scores is None:
        _novelty_scores = [0.0] * pop_size
    
    # Novelty weight: small constant
    novelty_weight = 0.001
    
    for _ in range(n_select):
        candidates = list(range(pop_size))
        cases = _case_order.copy()
        random.shuffle(cases)  # keep difficulty ordering but shuffle within difficulty? Actually we already have ordering.
        # For each case, apply epsilon-lexicase filter
        for case in cases:
            if len(candidates) <= 1:
                break
            case_errors = _errors[candidates, case]
            # Epsilon-lexicase with MAD threshold
            min_err = float(np.min(case_errors))
            mad = float(np.median(np.abs(case_errors - float(np.median(case_errors)))))
            candidates = [c for c, e in zip(candidates, case_errors) if e <= min_err + mad]
        
        # Among survivors, apply multi-criteria tie-breaking
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            # Combined score: fitness + parsimony*size - novelty_weight*novelty
            scores = []
            for c in candidates:
                score = fitnesses[c] + _parsimony_coeff * lengths[c] - novelty_weight * _novelty_scores[c]
                scores.append(score)
            winner = candidates[int(np.argmin(scores))]
        else:
            winner = candidates[0]
        selected.append(population[winner].copy())
    
    return selected


def crossover(parent1, parent2, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Standard subtree crossover."""
    offspring = parent1.copy()
    donor = parent2.copy()

    off_size = offspring.size()
    don_size = donor.size()
    if off_size <= 1 or don_size <= 1:
        return offspring

    off_point = random.randint(1, off_size - 1)
    don_point = random.randint(0, don_size - 1)

    donor_nodes = donor.get_all_nodes()
    donor_subtree = donor_nodes[don_point][0].copy()

    off_nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, parent, child_idx = off_nodes[off_point]
    if parent is not None:
        parent.children[child_idx] = donor_subtree
    else:
        offspring = donor_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent1.copy()

    return offspring


def mutation(parent, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Subtree mutation — replace a random subtree with a new random tree."""
    offspring = parent.copy()
    tree_size = offspring.size()
    if tree_size <= 1:
        return generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    mut_point = random.randint(1, tree_size - 1)
    new_subtree = generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, par, child_idx = nodes[mut_point]
    if par is not None:
        par.children[child_idx] = new_subtree
    else:
        offspring = new_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent.copy()

    return offspring


def evolve_one_generation(population, fitnesses, X_train, y_train,
                          n_features, pop_size,
                          crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.05,
                          max_depth=17):
    """Enhanced lexicase GP with difficulty ordering, novelty, and parsimony."""
    new_population = []
    
    # Elitism: keep best individual by raw fitness
    elite_idx = int(np.argmin(fitnesses))
    new_population.append(population[elite_idx].copy())
    
    # Compute per-case errors
    errors = _per_case_errors(population, X_train, y_train)
    
    # Compute case difficulties: median error across population
    case_difficulties = np.median(errors, axis=0)
    # Sort cases by difficulty descending (hardest first)
    case_order = np.argsort(-case_difficulties).tolist()
    
    # Compute novelty scores
    novelty_scores = _compute_novelty_scores(errors, k=10)
    
    # Adaptive parsimony coefficient (gplearn 'auto' method, clamped)
    lengths = np.array([tree.size() for tree in population], dtype=float)
    raw_fit = np.array(fitnesses, dtype=float)
    len_var = float(np.var(lengths))
    if len_var > 1e-15:
        parsimony_coeff = float(np.cov(lengths, raw_fit)[1, 0]) / len_var
        parsimony_coeff = max(parsimony_coeff, 0.0)
        parsimony_coeff = min(parsimony_coeff, 0.01)  # increased max
    else:
        parsimony_coeff = 0.0
    
    while len(new_population) < pop_size:
        r = random.random()
        if r < crossover_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 2, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _novelty_scores=novelty_scores)
            child = crossover(parents[0], parents[1], n_features, max_depth)
        elif r < crossover_rate + mutation_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _novelty_scores=novelty_scores)
            child = mutation(parents[0], n_features, max_depth)
        else:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _novelty_scores=novelty_scores)
            child = parents[0]
        new_population.append(child)
    
    return new_population[:pop_size]

def fitness_function(tree, X, y):
    """Evaluate fitness of a candidate program. Lower is better."""
    y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
    return float(np.mean((y - y_pred) ** 2))


def _per_case_errors(population, X, y):
    """Compute per-case absolute errors for the entire population.
    
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (len(population), n_samples)
    """
    errors = np.empty((len(population), X.shape[0]))
    for i, tree in enumerate(population):
        y_pred = safe_evaluate(tree, X)
        errors[i] = np.abs(y - y_pred)
    return errors


def selection(population, fitnesses, n_select, _errors=None, _parsimony_coeff=0.0,
              _case_order=None, _depths=None):
    """Enhanced epsilon-lexicase selection with depth penalty.
    
    Args:
        _errors: per-case error matrix
        _parsimony_coeff: coefficient for size penalty
        _case_order: list of case indices sorted by difficulty (hardest first)
        _depths: list of tree depths for each individual
    """
    selected = []
    pop_size = len(population)
    
    if _errors is None:
        # Fallback to tournament selection
        tournament_size = 7
        for _ in range(n_select):
            candidates = random.sample(range(pop_size), min(tournament_size, pop_size))
            best = min(candidates, key=lambda i: fitnesses[i])
            selected.append(population[best].copy())
        return selected
    
    n_cases = _errors.shape[1]
    lengths = [tree.size() for tree in population]
    if _depths is None:
        _depths = [tree.depth() for tree in population]
    
    # Default case order: random
    if _case_order is None:
        _case_order = list(range(n_cases))
    
    # Depth penalty weight (relative to size penalty)
    depth_weight = 0.1
    
    for _ in range(n_select):
        candidates = list(range(pop_size))
        cases = _case_order.copy()
        random.shuffle(cases)
        # Epsilon-lexicase filtering
        for case in cases:
            if len(candidates) <= 1:
                break
            case_errors = _errors[candidates, case]
            min_err = float(np.min(case_errors))
            mad = float(np.median(np.abs(case_errors - float(np.median(case_errors)))))
            candidates = [c for c, e in zip(candidates, case_errors) if e <= min_err + mad]
        
        # Tie-breaking with combined penalty: fitness + parsimony_coeff*(size + depth_weight*depth)
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            scores = []
            for c in candidates:
                penalty = _parsimony_coeff * (lengths[c] + depth_weight * _depths[c])
                scores.append(fitnesses[c] + penalty)
            winner = candidates[int(np.argmin(scores))]
        else:
            winner = candidates[0]
        selected.append(population[winner].copy())
    
    return selected


def crossover(parent1, parent2, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Standard subtree crossover."""
    offspring = parent1.copy()
    donor = parent2.copy()

    off_size = offspring.size()
    don_size = donor.size()
    if off_size <= 1 or don_size <= 1:
        return offspring

    off_point = random.randint(1, off_size - 1)
    don_point = random.randint(0, don_size - 1)

    donor_nodes = donor.get_all_nodes()
    donor_subtree = donor_nodes[don_point][0].copy()

    off_nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, parent, child_idx = off_nodes[off_point]
    if parent is not None:
        parent.children[child_idx] = donor_subtree
    else:
        offspring = donor_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent1.copy()

    return offspring


def mutation(parent, n_features, max_depth=17):
    """Subtree mutation — replace a random subtree with a new random tree."""
    offspring = parent.copy()
    tree_size = offspring.size()
    if tree_size <= 1:
        return generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    mut_point = random.randint(1, tree_size - 1)
    new_subtree = generate_tree('grow', 3, n_features)

    nodes = offspring.get_all_nodes()
    node, par, child_idx = nodes[mut_point]
    if par is not None:
        par.children[child_idx] = new_subtree
    else:
        offspring = new_subtree

    if offspring.depth() > max_depth:
        return parent.copy()

    return offspring


def evolve_one_generation(population, fitnesses, X_train, y_train,
                          n_features, pop_size,
                          crossover_rate=0.9, mutation_rate=0.05,
                          max_depth=17):
    """Enhanced lexicase GP with depth penalty and adaptive parsimony."""
    new_population = []
    
    # Elitism: keep best individual by raw fitness
    elite_idx = int(np.argmin(fitnesses))
    new_population.append(population[elite_idx].copy())
    
    # Compute per-case errors
    errors = _per_case_errors(population, X_train, y_train)
    
    # Compute case difficulties: median error across population
    case_difficulties = np.median(errors, axis=0)
    # Sort cases by difficulty descending (hardest first)
    case_order = np.argsort(-case_difficulties).tolist()
    
    # Compute depths
    depths = [tree.depth() for tree in population]
    
    # Adaptive parsimony coefficient (gplearn 'auto' method, clamped)
    lengths = np.array([tree.size() for tree in population], dtype=float)
    raw_fit = np.array(fitnesses, dtype=float)
    len_var = float(np.var(lengths))
    if len_var > 1e-15:
        parsimony_coeff = float(np.cov(lengths, raw_fit)[1, 0]) / len_var
        parsimony_coeff = max(parsimony_coeff, 0.0)
        parsimony_coeff = min(parsimony_coeff, 0.01)
    else:
        parsimony_coeff = 0.0
    
    while len(new_population) < pop_size:
        r = random.random()
        if r < crossover_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 2, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _depths=depths)
            child = crossover(parents[0], parents[1], n_features, max_depth)
        elif r < crossover_rate + mutation_rate:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _depths=depths)
            child = mutation(parents[0], n_features, max_depth)
        else:
            parents = selection(population, fitnesses, 1, _errors=errors,
                                _parsimony_coeff=parsimony_coeff,
                                _case_order=case_order,
                                _depths=depths)
            child = parents[0]
        new_population.append(child)
    
    return new_population[:pop_size]
